_comment: Aelgard boss design bible. Mirror of data/npc-bibles.json for boss encounters — mechanic summary, attack rotation, enrage phase, loot uniqueness. Supplements reports/boss-principle-audit.md (which rates code compliance) with DESIGN narration. The live NPC stat data lives in src/content/aelgard/bosses-expanded.js, raids-bosses-mega.js, raids-mega1/2.js, and bosses-principle-fixes.js. This file is the bible that the codex/narrator/raid-interface reads at runtime.
_audit_reference: reports/boss-principle-audit.md (87 bosses audited against 18 Scape-Builder-Injects principles; 1066/1566 cells violating; 15 top-priority patches applied)
_invocation_compatible: all entries include stat_shape and phase_markers so the raid-invocations subsystem can modulate them at runtime (HP multiplier, attack-speed, phase-thresholds)

_design_principles_shorthand.P14: asymmetric escalation (buff player, buff boss more)

bosses.name: Bryophyta
bosses.mechanic_summary: Moss giant queen; spawns growthling-rooted puddles under players every 6 ticks; puddles tether player to spot if stood on. Queen pulls player toward puddles via vine-grab on odd ticks.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: basic melee swing (max 14)
Tick 3: vine-grab on highest-HP player (pull 3 tiles toward boss)
Tick 6: growthling puddle spawn at furthest player's last known position
Tick 9: AoE moss-cloud (3-tile radius, damage reduces prayer points by 10)

enrage_phase.changes: attack_speed 4 -> 3; puddle spawn frequency doubles; vine-grab chains to 2 players

uniques.note: already an OSRS-analogue — stays the key mechanic

bosses.counterplay: magic weakness; run through puddles instead of around; face-tank vine-grabs with high def gear.

bosses.name: Obor
bosses.mechanic_summary: Hill giant capstone boss; throws 3-tile radius boulders every 7 ticks; boulders persist for 4 ticks as impassable terrain. Arena has 4 destructible pillars the boss can use for cover.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: heavy melee swing (max 16)
Tick 4: boulder throw (3-tile AoE, 4-tick persistence)
Tick 7: pillar crash (if adjacent to pillar, pillar collapses and stuns nearby players)

enrage_phase.changes: boulder frequency increases; boulders now stun on hit (1 tick)

uniques.note: sidegrade to granite maul — faster but lower max
reagent: 3 fragments + base club at Smith Kael = Boulder-clad Club (crush-niche vs construct-tag)

bosses.counterplay: stab weakness; do NOT stand behind pillars he can crash; boulder tiles block melee path, kite around them.

bosses.name: Sarachnis
bosses.mechanic_summary: Matriarch spider; spawns 2-3 spiderlings every 10 ticks that pursue player. Web-shoot attack tethers player for 2 ticks unless broken. Spiderlings heal boss if allowed to reach her.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: melee lunge (max 24)
Tick 4: web-shoot at furthest player (tether 2 ticks)
Tick 7: spiderling spawn (2-3 per wave)
Tick 10: AoE web-splash (prayer-drain 15 points)

enrage_phase.changes: spiderlings spawn 4 per wave; web-shoot hits all players on aggro list simultaneously

uniques.note: P12 — mid-tier slash weapon with passive spiderling-kill damage doubling

bosses.counterplay: slash weakness; PRIORITY — kill spiderlings before they reach boss (heal-loop mistake compounding, P05); web-tether can be broken with ranged hit or magic spell.

bosses.name: Skotizo
bosses.mechanic_summary: Catacombs altar-boss; uses 4 altars as power source (N/E/S/W). Unbroken altars grant Skotizo 75% damage reduction and 2x max hit. Players must dismantle altars during combat to become vulnerable.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: melee strike (max 14 base, 28 with altars)
Tick 4: dark shield absorb — next 2 hits on Skotizo dealt to random altar instead
Tick 7: altar-link lightning (if 2+ altars intact, lightning chains between altars through player position)

enrage_phase.changes: Skotizo fully vulnerable; attack_speed 5 -> 3; summons 2 demon-spawns

uniques.note: P11 — alt loadout: pairs with dark-claws-off weapon for paired-claw special attack

bosses.counterplay: multi-style resistance; designed for AoE damage to break altars while dodging altar-link lightning. Single-style parties struggle.

bosses.name: Duke Sucellus
bosses.mechanic_summary: Forge-Duke boss; seated on a throne that can be tipped via cardinal shockwaves. Arena has 4 gas vents. Gas vent eruptions force players to specific tiles while shockwave deals heavy damage.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: sword-thrust (max 22, melee range)
Tick 3: shockwave in a cardinal direction (tell: boss faces one direction for 2 ticks prior)
Tick 6: gas vent eruption (random 2 vents ignite, 3-tile radius, 31 damage)
Tick 10: throne-pound (stun radius 4 tiles from boss)

enrage_phase.changes: all 4 gas vents erupt simultaneously; shockwaves become diagonal instead of cardinal (harder to read direction)

uniques.note: reagent: + virtus body + nihil dust = Virtus magus robes (endgame magic)

bosses.counterplay: ranged weakness; shockwave direction telegraphed via boss-facing (P18 visual honesty); use tipped-throne phases to step in for burst.

bosses.name: Tempoross
bosses.mechanic_summary: Skilling-boss, not combat: Tempoross cannot be damaged by weapons. Players fish / cook / operate cannons cooperatively while it drains the boat's hit points. Failure sinks the boat; success awards fishing XP + unique tackle box drops.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: storm-gust AoE damage to boat (players must repair with planks)
Tick 5: vortex spawn (player must dodge; vortex pulls into sea)
Tick 8: wave-barrage (damages cannons, forces reload cycle)

enrage_phase.changes: storm-gust frequency doubles; vortex count 1 -> 3; cannons take double damage

uniques.note: unique: infinite water-rune source for autocasting

bosses.counterplay: community boss — team scaling; high fishing + firemaking levels are rewarded; the fight is a SKILL check, not a DPS check. P16-compliant (team unite).

bosses.name: The Leviathan
bosses.mechanic_summary: Sea-dragon; submerges mid-fight and sweeps the arena from one half at a time with its tail-breath. Players must reposition to unmarked half. Drains prayer on each sweep.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: melee bite (max 25 if in melee range)
Tick 4: ranged spear-throw (max 28)
Tick 8: submerge — mark half of arena, 2-tick warning, then sweep (max 33, prayer drain -25)

enrage_phase.changes: submerge sweep covers 3/4 of arena; only narrow corridor is safe

uniques.note: endgame special-attack-regen ring
reagent: + fishing rod = trawler-tier rod (Saltbrine endgame fishing)

bosses.counterplay: ranged weakness; sweep-direction telegraphed (P18); burst DPS during submerge startup.

bosses.name: Phantom Muspah
bosses.mechanic_summary: Shapeshifts between ranged (bow-phantom) and melee (sword-phantom) forms every 5 ticks. Prayer must match current form. Misread prayer = double damage.
attack_rotation: Tick 1 (ranged phase): bow volley (max 32, ranged defense matters)
Tick 5: shapeshift — visible aura-color change (blue -> red)
Tick 6 (melee phase): rapid claw-strike (max 28, melee defense)
Tick 10: shapeshift back

enrage_phase.changes: shapeshift every 3 ticks instead of 5; adds magic form (yellow aura) as third rotation

uniques.note: reagent: 5 shards + magic shortbow = venator bow (prayer-defense-ignoring ranged — niche)

bosses.counterplay: aura-color is the prayer cue (P18 visual honesty); high multi-style defense loadouts trivialize the fight — but cost effective supplies.

bosses.name: The Whisperer
bosses.mechanic_summary: Dual-plane boss: half of the fight in the waking world, half in the dream-world. Players must enter dream-portal mid-combat to deal real damage; outside the portal, only 20% damage lands.
attack_rotation: Tick 1 (waking): magic dart (max 20, ranged defense)
Tick 4 (waking): dream-portal opens (3-tile rune-circle telegraph)
Player enters dream (tick 5-12): inside dream, Whisperer attacks with tendril (max 34, magic defense), 100% damage dealt by player
Tick 13: player forced back to waking

enrage_phase.changes: dream-portal stays open for only 4 ticks (shorter window); tendril attack frequency doubles inside dream

uniques.note: reagent: + virtus robes + nihil dust = virtus robes (endgame magic set)

bosses.counterplay: stab weakness; portal-cycle timing matters more than raw DPS. Classic plane-shift mechanic, P01 multiple optimal actions (enter portal or stack-heal outside).

bosses.name: Crystal Wyrm
bosses.mechanic_summary: Three-phase Veilwood dragon with crystallite pillars and arena-glass hazards. Most principle-compliant boss in the audit — pillars are interactive entities, phases teach-then-combine.
attack_rotation: Phase 1 (100-66% HP): magic breath, crystallite minion spawns (2 per wave, focus-fire kills)
Phase 2 (66-33% HP): arena shatters into mirror-glass; refract attacks from any angle; must hide behind intact pillars
Phase 3 (33-0% HP): enrage + blitz; wyrm flies between pillars; only ranged attacks land

enrage_phase.changes: flight mode — only ranged/magic hit; pillar-shelter timer halved

uniques.note: reagent: + refracted_essence = Crystal Bane (slayer-niche vs crystal-tag)

bosses.counterplay: stab weakness; phase-2 is the teach moment for pillar-shelter mechanic; phase-3 rewards ranged loadout.

bosses.name: Nex
bosses.mechanic_summary: Endgame 5-phase GWD-tier boss: Smoke / Shadow / Blood / Ice / Zaros phase sequence. Each phase requires a different prayer and protection scheme. Minion-kill required to progress between phases.
attack_rotation: Phase 1 (Smoke): AoE smoke volley, protect from missiles; minion: Fumus (summons smoke pools)
Phase 2 (Shadow): shadow clones of party, protect from magic; minion: Umbra
Phase 3 (Blood): vampiric heal on unprotected hits, protect from melee; minion: Cruor
Phase 4 (Ice): freeze + shatter (moving = max 38); minion: Glacies
Phase 5 (Zaros): all-style enrage; no specific prayer works — damage race

enrage_phase.changes: player_damage_multiplier x1.25 (P14 asymmetric — reward for reaching phase 5); boss_damage_multiplier x2.0

uniques.note: reagent: + vambraces base = enhanced vambraces

bosses.counterplay: P11 strategic plurality — 3-style prayer-switching loadout OR single-style tank-through-smoke speedrun; both viable. Flag P17 concern: gated behind 5-phase clear in quest chain — now addressed via practice-mode instance in phase-3 training room.

bosses.name: Vardorvis
bosses.mechanic_summary: Rotating axe arena boss; 4 giant axes orbit the room in 2 directions. Player stands on designated 'safe path' tiles. Heal-on-stand healing pools spawn on incorrect tile choices (P05 compounding mistake).
attack_rotation: Tick 1: melee cleave (max 35 if in melee)
Tick 3: axe-rotation tick (orbit advances one tile)
Tick 6: heal-pool spawn (random tile; Vardorvis heals +10 HP if player stands on it for 2 ticks)
Tick 9: root attack (tethers player for 2 ticks; axes still move)

enrage_phase.changes: axe-rotation every 2 ticks instead of 3; heal-pool spawns accelerate

uniques.note: reagent: + rune axe = Executioner's Axe (slayer-niche vs undead + shade)

bosses.counterplay: stab weakness; axe-tile tracking is the puzzle; root+heal-pool timing is the compounding-mistake test (P05).

bosses.name: Sol Heredit
bosses.mechanic_summary: 3-style champion with grapple and shield-bash specials. Prayer must match weapon style he's currently using. Grapple pulls player into melee range at random tick. Shield-bash stuns player 1 tick.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: melee strike (sword-form, max 34)
Tick 4: ranged spear-throw (bow-form, max 32)
Tick 7: magic bolt (staff-form, max 36)
Tick 10: grapple (pull 5 tiles toward boss)
Tick 12: shield-bash (stun, break combo)

enrage_phase.changes: style rotation every 2 ticks instead of 3; adds feint — fake weapon-change, attack arrives as previous style

uniques.note: provides infinite ammunition + 5% range accuracy

bosses.counterplay: P11 plurality — multi-style prayer-switch OR damage-race with dizana's quiver power-creep; grapple-counter = anti-grapple charms from Heartlands shop.

bosses.name: Pharaoh Lich (Boss)
bosses.mechanic_summary: Boneyard capstone. Summons a clerical staff of reanimated mummy-wardens who issue 'decrees' — each decree is a constraint the player must obey for 10 ticks, or take heavy damage. E.g., 'Decree: the Pharaoh demands silence' — casting spells incurs damage; 'Decree: the Pharaoh demands stillness' — moving deals 10 damage per step.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: staff blast (max 22, magic)
Tick 4: decree announcement (random from 4 constraints, active for 10 ticks)
Tick 6: bone-pile eruption (8 bone-swarm spawns, each does 3 damage on pickup)

enrage_phase.changes: two decrees active simultaneously; bone-piles explode on kill instead of harmless

uniques.note: reagent: + base_diadem = Sand-crown diadem (mummy-niche BiS)
ignores 20% magic defense on mummy-tag targets

bosses.counterplay: stab weakness; decree-reading is the core skill (P01 plurality — accept decree and take damage, or adapt loadout); bone-pile management is a mini-logistics puzzle.

bosses.name: The Forgotten-Name
bosses.mechanic_summary: Inkweald endgame boss. Unique mechanic: the boss's NAME cannot be spoken aloud. The in-game boss-timer and damage-log display '————' in place of the name. Combat itself uses attack-style swapping and reality-fold attacks that phase the player in/out of the dream plane.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: reality-fold (phase player out of dream plane — deals damage only inside dream; tick 2 phase them back)
Tick 4: forget-strike (max 25, cannot be prayed against without knowing the name)
Tick 7: name-inversion (player's equipped weapon display blanks for 5 ticks)
Tick 10: dream-wall (wall of unnamed memory sweeps across arena, impassable)

enrage_phase.changes: reality-fold every 2 ticks; name-inversion permanent until kill (weapon stats still apply, just the display is blank)

uniques.note: UNNAMEABLE item — the only item whose name cannot be spoken in-game. Confers prayer-pool bonus unique to this one item. Pillar 4 exemplar.

bosses.counterplay: ranged weakness; phase-timing (enter dream during fold-phase, burst DPS, retreat); the 'unknowable' mechanic is dialog-telegraphed via Inkweald NPC Daranda who describes the fight without naming.

bosses._bible_source: [v0.9-waveC2] M3 — 10 most-fought bosses upgraded from stat-block to bible
bosses.name: Vorkath
bosses.voice: a long-dead dragon that no longer thinks — it remembers. Roars are syllables of an older draconic tongue and each acid-volley hisses a single word the player cannot quite hear. Its breath carries the cold of a grave that was buried in ash, then re-sealed.

drives.wants: to finish the sentence it started before the old king killed it
drives.fears: being forgotten completely (losing the last of its remembered self)
drives.secret: three of its scales are still tuned to the bells of Castle Malachar and ring faintly when a true heir approaches

bosses.ecology: Vorkath sleeps inside a barrow cut into the northern cliffs of Moryskah. Soulfen gravediggers report its scales occasionally surfacing in the mire kilometers away. It drains no life when dormant; it drains the COLOUR from the surrounding grass in a 30m ring, which is why the approach is grey even in summer.
bosses.mechanic_summary: Ice-and-fire undead dragon that cycles six special attacks on a loop (acid pools, fire dragonbreath, ice breath freeze, venom spit, zombie-spawn, and a fourth-wall-special: the 'Ascension Bomb' which requires prayer-flick or instant death). Arena floor accumulates acid pools that never despawn — a long fight strangles the player's footprint.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: standard dragonbreath (pray mage)
Tick 4: standard dragonbreath OR ranged spike (pray ranged)
Every 6th special slot: ONE of [acid pool spawn, fire-wall pattern, freeze breath, venom volley, zombie-spawn]
Every 7th special: Ascension Bomb (big yellow orb — prayer-flick to opposite style on the tick it connects, or take 100+ damage)
bosses.rotation_notes: Specials cycle in a deterministic order and skip the last-used. Players learn the 5-special pattern, not RNG. Zombie-spawn phase requires either crumble-undead cast (magic) or a salve-tag ranged weapon — Pillar 11 plurality. Pool placement is fixed-random: first pool at 80% HP, then every ~45 seconds.

enrage_phase.changes: Ascension Bomb frequency doubles; acid pools now spread 1 tile per tick; spawn-phase summons zombie-spawns at +1 per cycle

uniques.note: mountable in POH; ticks when a true heir is in the house
reagent: visage + draconic anvil = Draconic Visage equivalent, unlocks Dragonfire Shield craft

bosses.loot_philosophy: Vorkath is the mid-game profit anchor — high GP/hr, no uniques required for progression, but the Skeletal Visage gates an endgame shield craft. Every kill leaves the player objectively richer; Pillar 9 (reward a finite game) hits because the visage roll is THE memorable moment, not the coin pile.
bosses.counterplay: crumble-undead + ranged swap loadout is BiS; Zulrah-style prayer-flick on Ascension Bomb required; walking between acid pools matters more than DPS past 50% HP.

bosses.name: Zulrah
bosses.voice: speaks only in hiss-patterns that priestesses of the Tidemother claim are numbers. Never repeats a hiss-pattern in a single fight. The pattern-sequence is the ONLY language of the fight — and it is taught visually, not audibly: the player learns Zulrah by watching Zulrah, not by being told.

drives.fears: being permanently understood (the moment a player knows every rotation, Zulrah is already planning the next mutation)
drives.secret: a fourth form exists that no player has triggered in recorded history; it requires all three existing forms to be killed without player-damage in a single fight

bosses.ecology: Zulrah rises from a single swamp-poisoned saline well in Saltbrine's southern marsh. The well's water doesn't evaporate; frogs born in its radius are always the same three patterns of colour — green, red, blue. Saltbrine Reach fishers will not eat from the well's watershed. The well is stable; Zulrah's cycle is every 48 hours, without exception.
bosses.mechanic_summary: Three-form phase boss: Green (range, poison clouds), Blue (magic, venom-storm), Red (melee + ranged, spawns snakelings). Each form locks out one combat style and demands two-item-slot switching. The player is doing two things simultaneously: reading the rotation AND switching gear faster than the tick cycle.
attack_rotation: Green form: range attacks + toxic smoke clouds (pray range; avoid clouds)
Blue form: magic attacks + venom storm (pray magic; run through clear tile every 4 ticks)
Red form: range + melee + spawns snakelings (prioritize snakelings OR tank them with salve amulet)
Rotation: random seed per fight, but form-sequence is ALWAYS green->red->green->blue or green->blue->green->red etc — never two same-form in a row
bosses.rotation_notes: Fight duration is fixed: ~5 minutes at max efficiency, ~9 minutes at learner pace. Sub-3-minute kills exist but require 4-way switching under ticks. Pillar 8 roguelite modifier: Invocations can lock rotation to one-form-only for a +150% loot multiplier on that form's unique.

enrage_phase.changes: phase-transition speed increases (was every 50 HP, now every 30); snakeling spawn increases by 1 per transition

uniques.note: cosmetic — recolours Magic Fang; Pillar 2 prestige item
reagent: + toxic_trident_base = BiS mage off-hand
reagent: + blowpipe_base = toxic blowpipe
reagent: + crafting work = serpentine helm (venom-proof)

bosses.loot_philosophy: Zulrah is the scale economy. Every kill drips small profit; rare uniques gate mid-tier weapon crafts (blowpipe, trident, serpentine helm). The mutagens are cosmetic-only — Pillar 2 confirms that prestige-without-power is still a valid reward. Players farm Zulrah for the rotation mastery, not the coins.
bosses.counterplay: 3-style gear swap + prayer flick cycle; new players die most often to ignoring snakelings in red-phase; the well's location is quest-gated via the_trawlers_call.

bosses.name: Shadow-Muspah
bosses.voice: entirely silent. Its signature 'sound' is the absence of the dream's ambient drone — when Shadow-Muspah steps onto the arena tile, the Inkweald ambient music stops and the player hears only their own character's footsteps. This silence IS the telegraph.

drives.wants: nothing (Shadow-Muspah does not want; it completes patterns)
drives.fears: incomplete patterns (will ignore its own enrage to finish a spawn cycle)
drives.secret: is not actually alive — is a residual echo left by a traveler who died mid-quest. The quest that traveler failed is findable in the Inkweald archives as an unfinished journal entry.

bosses.ecology: Shadow-Muspah manifests in a loop at the deep-dream Resonance Chamber. It does not hunt, eat, or sleep; it arrives, performs its four-phase pattern, despawns, and re-arrives exactly 17 minutes later. The wall of the chamber is carved with tally-marks left by everyone who has died to it; the tally is 2,404 marks deep.
bosses.mechanic_summary: Four-phase encounter: (1) Ranged-shield phase — melee and mage immune; (2) Magic-shield phase — melee and ranged immune; (3) Melee-shield phase — mage and ranged immune; (4) Prayer-drain blitz phase — must use lunar ancestry to prevent drain. The wrong style does ZERO damage; players carry all three combat styles at once.
attack_rotation: Phase 1 (range-shielded): basic ranged attacks from boss, player must mage/melee
Phase 2 (magic-shielded): basic magic attacks, player must range/melee
Phase 3 (melee-shielded): melee cleave + stomp, player must range/mage
Phase 4 (no shield, prayer-blitz): full damage taken from all styles; boss attacks drain prayer 5 pts per hit
bosses.rotation_notes: Phase transitions are HP-gated at 75/50/25% and a brief 'shroud sequence' separates phases — during shroud, boss is invulnerable and teleports to opposite side of arena. Pillar 1 multiple-optimal-actions: some teams clear shroud phases by pre-positioning instead of kiting.

enrage_phase.changes: prayer drain doubles to 10 pts/hit; adds a self-stomp that deals 15 damage to boss AND player every 4 ticks — race to kill

uniques.note: reagent: 3 icons = ancient_sceptre; Pillar 10 — iconic weapon with ancient-magicks spec
consumable; grants 1 use of ice-barrage at half cost
reagent: 4 shards + crafting = venator bow (ranged BIS hybrid)

bosses.loot_philosophy: Muspah is a reagent boss. Every drop is a FRAGMENT; the player needs ~3-4 runs to assemble a complete upgrade. This pacing keeps the boss relevant for longer than a one-roll BiS fight. Pillar 13 — the journey of acquiring uniques is long and punctuated by small wins.
bosses.counterplay: three-style gear swap (magic + ranged + melee in one kit); lunar prayer book recommended for Phase 4; wave-learn from NPC Daranda before first attempt.

bosses.name: The Wake-Warden (Kraken-analog)
bosses.voice: does not speak above water. Under water, the arena audio is REPLACED by deep-sea whalesong that ocean-priestesses say is the Warden humming a forgotten harbour-song. The song has a verse and a chorus; the chorus coincides with its lethal whirlpool attack.

drives.wants: to remember the names of every ship it ever broke
drives.fears: rain (its tentacles retract when fresh water falls — it can be rained OUT of a fight by weather invocations)
drives.secret: a sunken bell at the bottom of the arena, if rung, will cause the Warden to surface willingly and not attack for 10 ticks — a secret mercy

bosses.ecology: The Wake-Warden lives in Saltbrine's cursed waters, in a flooded subterranean temple connected to the harbour only by an underwater shortcut (60 agility). It feeds on sound, not flesh — every ship that has ever sunk in Saltbrine lost its bell to the Warden. Fisher-guild accountants have the manifest and know.
bosses.mechanic_summary: Single-style magic boss, but the arena is submerged and the player has a 60-tick air-timer. Four tentacles emerge in a cross pattern; killing tentacles opens direct hits on the body. Tentacles regenerate every 25 ticks. Player rotates DPS between the body (slow) and tentacles (fast regen).
attack_rotation: Tick 1-3: standard magic-burst attacks from body (pray magic)
Tick 4: whirlpool spawn — forces player to move, tentacles attack from new range
Tick 7: tentacle slam on lowest-HP player (bypasses protect)
Tick 10: harbour-song chorus — 4-tile arena-wide shockwave; must be behind a tentacle to avoid
bosses.rotation_notes: Pillar 11 plurality: AFK-magic-only kills work but take 3x longer; dedicated melee + tentacle-kiting runs in half the time. Players pick the style. Air-timer creates tension that single-style bosses lack.

enrage_phase.changes: tentacle regen doubles; harbour-song chorus fires every 6 ticks instead of 10; whirlpools persist 4 ticks longer

uniques.note: reagent: + abyssal whip = whip-tentacle; Pillar 4 equipment continuity from pre-endgame
reagent: + fire staff + 20k coins + craft at magic guild = trident_of_the_seas; one of the starter endgame magic weapons

bosses.loot_philosophy: Kraken is the 'first endgame' boss — low combat requirement but high reward. Tentacle drop pushes whip users to their next tier (whip-tentacle) without obsoleting the whip. Pillar 4 — old content upgrades are always combinations, never replacements.
bosses.counterplay: air-management is THE skill (bring stamina + magic defense); the bell secret rewards exploration-minded players with a 10-tick free phase; agility shortcut at 60 saves 2 minutes per trip.

bosses.name: The Hellwatch Hound (Cerberus-analog)
bosses.voice: growls have words in them, but the words are names — names of everyone who has entered the gate and not come back. If the player listens at the approach without drawing weapons, they will hear their own name whispered once.

drives.wants: to complete its Watch (has been guarding the gate for longer than Aelgard has had a calendar)
drives.fears: being replaced by a younger hound (takes this very personally)
drives.secret: the gate it guards has been unlocked for 200 years — but it has never tried the door

bosses.ecology: Lives at the Wilds level-40 gate to the catacombs-of-the-forgotten. Does not hunt; does not eat; does not sleep; does not leave its 8-tile patrol square. When slain, a lesser hellhound takes the Watch within 60 ticks. No boss in Aelgard has been slain as many times as this one.
bosses.mechanic_summary: Three-headed hound with a core mechanic: each head uses a different combat style, and killing one head makes the boss enrage. Players must DPS all three heads simultaneously using a tri-style swap, OR bait each head into its own punish-phase using specific consumables (prayer potion, ranging potion, magic potion).
attack_rotation: Head 1 (melee): lunge + bite every 4 ticks
Head 2 (ranged): ember-spit (max 20) every 4 ticks
Head 3 (magic): shadow-bolt (max 22) every 5 ticks
Every 10 ticks: SOUL FLAMES — three pillars rise at cardinal points; player must stand in the pillar that matches the last attack style to prevent heal-back (Pillar 5 compounding mistake)
bosses.rotation_notes: Soul-flame mistake is the compounding fail: miss pillar, boss heals 20 HP. Two consecutive misses resets boss to 100% HP. Pillar 5 exemplar — one mistake is OK, two is deadly. Pillar 1 plurality: tri-style gear kit vs single-style prayer-flick both work at different skill ceilings.

enrage_phase.changes: pillar-flame interval drops to every 6 ticks; each head's attack speed drops by 1 tick; misplaced pillar now heals boss 40 HP

uniques.note: reagent: + dragon_boots = primordial boots (melee BiS); Pillar 4 old-content upgrade
reagent: + ranger_boots = pegasian boots (ranged BiS)
reagent: + infinity_boots = eternal boots (magic BiS)
reagent: imbues boot-tier for +2 prayer bonus

bosses.loot_philosophy: Hellwatch is the boot-tier gate. Three crystal types = three style BiS boots = three separate player-pursuit rewards. Pillar 11 strategic plurality: main-style players chase one crystal, hybrid players chase all three. Boot upgrades are incremental; the journey is the reward.
bosses.counterplay: slayer level 91 required (gate mechanic); bring prayer potions heavily — pillar-flame punishment scales with mistakes; learn the sound of each head's wind-up (each has a different growl-pitch).

bosses.name: The Smouldering Priest (Thermonuclear-analog)
bosses.voice: speaks through the forge-heat — voice carried on rising smoke, always in the second person, always in the player's native accent (the code reads ui_language_hint to localize the voice). Says only prophetic two-sentence pairs, never addresses the player by name.

drives.wants: to ascend (the smoke is its attempt to leave the forge bodily; it almost makes it every time)
drives.fears: the forge going cold (its corporeal form depends on ambient heat)
drives.secret: was the first forge-priest of Sootworks, cursed by the old deep-mine spirits; knows where the first vein is and will whisper it to any player who spares it after it reaches 5% HP (a secret mercy branch)

bosses.ecology: The Priest haunts the upper-level forge hall after dusk. By day the area is a working smithy; by night the anvils move on their own. Sootworks management has blacklisted the area from unionized hours. The Priest does not feed; it consumes smoke, and the forge fires dim in a 15m radius around its arena.
bosses.mechanic_summary: Magic-only boss that fills the arena with smoke clouds. Smoke degrades player visibility (sprites fade) and slowly burns (1 HP/tick while inside). Arena has 4 forge-vents that can be activated to CLEAR smoke for 10 ticks — but activating a vent also buffs the boss's magic damage by +5 for 20 ticks. Trade-off: visibility vs incoming damage.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: shadow-flame magic burst (max 28)
Tick 4: smoke-volley (6 clouds spawn around arena, each 2-tile radius)
Tick 7: ash-rain (AoE from above, telegraphed 2 ticks in advance)
Tick 10: forge-slam (melee range stomp — hitting player in arena periphery)
bosses.rotation_notes: Pillar 4 threats interact: smoke clouds BLOCK visibility AND degrade accuracy, so DPS suffers in smoke; venting fixes visibility but makes hits harder. No free win. Pillar 1 optimal action is contextual: late-fight with low HP, you want smoke (tank vents), high HP you want vented arena.

enrage_phase.changes: smoke-volley becomes constant (arena fully smoked until boss death); forge-slam now deals AoE 4 tiles

uniques.note: magic damage +10%; BiS neck slot for mage until fang-neck crafts
reagent: + mystic_steam = smoke_battlestaff_mystic; unique to this boss, magic damage + fire/smoke spell autocast

bosses.loot_philosophy: Thermy is the magic-damage gate. Occult necklace roll feels like a promotion: one kill and your magic DPS jumps a tier. Pillar 9 finite-reward: the necklace will NEVER be obsoleted (endgame amulets stack on top, not replace).
bosses.counterplay: 85 slayer required; bring high magic defense; vent-management is a skill trained over many kills; the 'spare it' branch is missed by 90% of players first-try.

bosses.name: General Ferrick (Graardor-analog)
bosses.voice: shouts orders in a pidgin soldier-tongue that's half Heartlands-barracks-slang and half ogre-roar. Names his three minions by role, never by name: 'Mace', 'Ranger', 'Mage'. If any minion is killed, the General mourns them for exactly one tick before resuming combat.

drives.wants: to find a general worth losing to (has defeated every challenger)
drives.fears: abandonment (his minions ARE his self-worth; if all three fall he enters a grief-berserk phase)
drives.secret: writes poetry in a notebook in the back of the throne room. The notebook is a readable object and one of the Wilds' hidden lore items.

bosses.ecology: Ferrick commands the Iron Company, a four-member war-retinue holed up in a fortified stronghold in the deep Wilds. The Iron Company does not raid; they fortify. The stronghold is sealed against all but bearers of the ogre-charter-key. Ferrick has occupied the stronghold for 34 in-game years.
bosses.mechanic_summary: God-Wars style boss+3 minions fight. General hits hardest but minions cover 3 styles (melee mace, ranged bolts, magic bolts). Killing minions is punished by a grief-phase. The key insight: minions DO NOT respawn. Once killed, the General is ALONE and enrages massively.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: General — heavy melee swing (max 32)
Tick 2: Mace minion — melee swing (max 18)
Tick 3: Ranger minion — crossbow bolt (max 15)
Tick 4: Mage minion — shadow bolt (max 19)
Every 8 ticks: General throws a boulder (4-tile AoE, max 28)
bosses.rotation_notes: Pillar 11 plurality: kill minions for a 'lonely general' burst phase (deadly but short), or leave them alive and bleed the General down slowly. Speed runners do the former; safe runners do the latter. Pillar 14 asymmetric escalation: when all 3 minions die, the General's attack speed drops from 6 to 4 AND max hit jumps to 45.

enrage_phase.changes: attack_speed 6 -> 4; max_hit 32 -> 45; gains an uninterruptible 'final charge' ability that deals 90 damage over 3 ticks in a line across the arena

uniques.note: melee BiS body slot (equipped as Ferrick's surrendered plate)
melee BiS legs slot
melee BiS boots
reagent: + godsword_blade = bandos_godsword; arena godsword special

bosses.loot_philosophy: GWD tier is the melee progression wall — bandos chestplate/tassets are the first full-tier melee BiS pieces. The 1/381 drop rate is BRUTAL; grinding is the content, not the kill itself. Pillar 13 — the long roll IS the game-mode.
bosses.counterplay: 70 strength required (stronghold door); team setups of 4 divide attention across minions; solo players tank the General while killing minions in a set order (Mage -> Ranger -> Mace).

bosses.name: Saint Zilvara (Zilyana-analog)
bosses.voice: preaches in Old Aelgardi throughout the fight, quoting scripture at each attack. Knows every player's canonical quest achievements and references specific completed quests aloud (uses event-log lookups to name-drop). Never cruel; always disappointed.

drives.wants: to convert the world back to the Dawnspear faith (believes she is losing)
drives.fears: being remembered as a warrior and not a saint
drives.secret: her three commanders are her actual biological children; the church marriage records are hidden in Heartlands archives

bosses.ecology: Zilvara holds the Dawnspear chapel-fortress in the deep Wilds, inherited from her mother. The chapel houses the Tear-of-Light relic that powers Dawnspear miracles. Three of her commanders guard the entrance; she receives pilgrims daily but only fights challengers. In-game, her respawn is the shortest in the Wilds — 42 ticks.
bosses.mechanic_summary: Fast hybrid boss with 3 minion-commanders. Each commander specializes: one in healing (heals Zilvara), one in ranged, one in magic. Zilvara hits both melee and magic. Critical trick: the healer commander MUST die first or the fight is unwinnable. But the healer is protected by the other two.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: Zilvara — magic smite (max 19)
Tick 2: Zilvara — melee sword cut (max 27)
Tick 4: healer-commander — AoE heal on team (Zilvara + allies +15 HP)
Tick 5: ranger-commander — crossbow (max 14)
Tick 6: mage-commander — magic bolt (max 16)
bosses.rotation_notes: Pillar 1 plurality: rush-healer strategy requires a 2-item-slot switch kit; tank-everything strategy requires full magic-def armour. Team setups distribute the healer-kill, ranger-kill, mage-kill across members. Solo is HARD. Pillar 5 compounding: every extra second the healer survives = 15 HP of heal on Zilvara = fight extension.

enrage_phase.changes: Zilvara gains +1 attack speed; if healer still alive, heals scale from 15 -> 35 HP per pulse

uniques.note: ranged BiS legs
ranged-def BiS body
reagent: + godsword_blade = saradomin_godsword (heals on spec)
ranged BiS crossbow until zaryte-tier

bosses.loot_philosophy: Dawnspear is the ranged progression wall. The saradomin godsword heals on spec — Pillar 9 reward: it IS a BiS, but it's a BiS with UTILITY (heals 50% of damage dealt on spec). Players keep it in their bank forever, even after zaryte unlocks.
bosses.counterplay: 70 agility required (chapel walls); bring ranged-def armour; healer-first strategy demands precision; crossbow drop keeps the boss worth farming even after saradomin-plate roll.

bosses.name: K'ruul Deathmark (K'ril-analog)
bosses.voice: speaks in demonic-grammar — subject-verb-object inverted. 'Your soul, I take' not 'I take your soul'. Addresses the player as 'little-mortal-with-god-inside'. Only boss in Aelgard who recognizes divine-tier invocations and changes dialogue for each.

drives.wants: to return to the primordial demon plane (has been trapped in Aelgard for centuries)
drives.fears: purification rituals (refuses to enter consecrated ground; this is a counter-play mechanic)
drives.secret: has a sibling who is a boss in Veilwood (future quest content will link them)

bosses.ecology: K'ruul commands a deep-Wilds demon-legion outpost. Unlike Ferrick/Zilvara, his minions are bonded to him by blood-pact — if K'ruul dies, minions auto-despawn. This makes him the 'kill-the-head' boss of the Wilds GWD trio. His legion is 14 demons strong but only 3 are in the arena at a time.
bosses.mechanic_summary: Fast hybrid boss with 3 demon-minions and a prayer-drain signature attack. K'ruul himself can hit 45 on a lucky poison-spec. Demons specialize in melee, magic, and 'soul-siphon' (prayer drain). The soul-siphon is THE fight: mages lose prayer points fast, and running out of prayer = melee-burst death.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: K'ruul — demonic-melee (max 30)
Tick 2: K'ruul — shadow-magic (max 25)
Tick 4: melee-demon — cleave (max 22)
Tick 5: soul-siphon demon — drains 10 prayer pts
Tick 6: magic-demon — blood-bolt (max 20, heals K'ruul for 50% of damage dealt)
bosses.rotation_notes: Pillar 4 threats interact: soul-siphon forces low-prayer state, which removes your protect-from-melee, which lets K'ruul's 30-max-melee rip through. The 'right answer' is piety + smite on soul-demon first. But smite costs prayer. So the PRE-fight loadout is the test. Pillar 11 plurality: restore-prayer-flask builds vs smite-rush builds are both viable.

enrage_phase.changes: K'ruul's attacks gain 30% lifesteal; soul-siphon doubles to 20 pts drain; blood-bolt heal scales to 75%

uniques.note: reagent: + godsword_blade = zamorak_godsword (ice-barrage spec)
reagent: + magic_fang = toxic_staff_of_the_dead; Pillar 4 cross-boss upgrade chain
fire + water combo staff
stab-niche BiS for specific raid encounters

bosses.loot_philosophy: K'ruul is the MAGIC progression wall. Staff of the Dead + Magic Fang cross-boss combo (upgrade from Zulrah drop) is Pillar 4 in action — old content stays alive because its drops combine with this content's drops. Pillar 10 iconic — the SotD's name is known even to non-bossers.
bosses.counterplay: 70 hitpoints required (blood-pact door); smite-rush the soul-siphon demon first; prayer flasks are non-negotiable; consecrated weapons (from Dawnspear rep) deal +15% to K'ruul.

bosses.name: The Oldwyrm (King Black Dragon-analog)
bosses.voice: does not speak to the player directly; its 'voice' is the rumble of the mountain around it. When it awakens, the entire Wilds shakes — every player in the region sees a tremor animation. Its only vocal noise is a long inhale before each breath.

drives.wants: to sleep longer (has been awakened 40,000 times; is tired)
drives.fears: young dragons (scared they will eclipse it)
drives.secret: guards a hoard of letters — not treasure; a library of every letter ever sent through the Wilds, curated over millennia; some letters are readable lore items

bosses.ecology: The Oldwyrm rules the deepest cave under the Wilds' western peaks. Its respawn timer is 30 ticks — it's the Wilds' 'farmable' boss, the entry-level dragon experience. Despite being farmable, it's geographically ancient: its cave predates recorded Aelgard history.
bosses.mechanic_summary: Classic three-style dragonbreath boss. Standard attacks in melee range; dragonbreath at range requiring antifire potion. The skill check is simple: do you have antifire, super-antifire, or extended-antifire? The gear-tier check is the fight. Low combat reqs, accessible solo, first 'real' boss for most new players.
attack_rotation: Tick 1: melee bite (if in melee range, max 14)
Tick 4: dragonbreath (ranged, max 65 WITHOUT antifire, max 10 WITH antifire)
Tick 7: tail-swipe (AoE 3 tiles around boss, max 20)
Tick 10: triple-breath (fire + ice + poison in sequence — requires full-antifire + venom-protection)
bosses.rotation_notes: Pillar 2 learnable: this is the 'textbook' dragon fight. Every subsequent dragon-style boss builds on this pattern. Triple-breath is the ONE exotic mechanic — teaches players about combined-style dragonbreath before they encounter Vorkath's Ascension Bomb later.

enrage_phase.changes: dragonbreath frequency doubles; tail-swipe knocks back 2 tiles (disrupts melee DPS window)

uniques.note: reagent: + 250k coins + anvil work = dragonfire_shield; Pillar 4 shield upgrade path
mountable in POH; grants +1 prayer bonus when near
lore item — readable, reveals a letter the Oldwyrm preserved

bosses.loot_philosophy: KBD is the tutorial-boss. The draconic_visage is a 1/5000 chase item that CARRIES players through their first 500 kills. The true prize is the POH trophy — prestige reward (Pillar 2), not power. Players who farm this long enough get the shield; players who do it once leave with the story.
bosses.counterplay: antifire mandatory (super-antifire ideal); melee + crush weapon works; solo-able from combat level 100+; triple-breath is the 'welcome to bosses' mechanic for intermediate players.
